newsitem.title: CHILE: South Korean leader arrives in Chile.
newsitem.headline: South Korean leader arrives in Chile.

text.p: South Korean President Kim Young-sam arrived in Chile on Thursday for a three-day official visit as part of a five-nation tour of Latin America aimed at strengthening trade with the region.
Kim did not speak to reporters on his arrival from Guatemala at Santiago's international airport where he was met by Foreign Minister Jose Miguel Insulza.
Chile is the second stop on the South Korean leader's 12-day tour of the region and will be followed by visits to Argentina, Brazil and Peru.
Kim, who is being accompanied by 42 business leaders, will hold talks with President Eduardo Frei on Friday and attend the closing ceremony of a seminar for businessmen from both countries.
South Korea is keen to boost its investments in Chile's forestry, infrastructure, telecommunications and mining sectors.
"These are the areas which have been defined as high priority and interest for the development and growth of trade relations between Chile and Korea," said the Chile-Korea business committee.
Top Korean industrial conglomerate Hyundai Corp. announced last week it would spend $300 million to build a joint venture copper refinery in Chile, which is the world's largest copper producer.
Trade between the two countries is rising sharply and totaled $1.4 billion last year, up 160 percent in the last three years.
